questions.q: What is the difference between a scalar function and a table-returning function?
options: A scalar function returns a single value; a table-returning function returns a result set you can query like a table
A scalar function can only be called from a WHERE clause
A table-returning function can only return one row
There is no real difference between the two
questions.explain: Scalar functions return one value (a number, string, date); table-returning functions return a result set usable in a FROM clause.

questions.q: What is the genuine platform limitation this lesson names for MySQL?
options: MySQL has no true table-valued function concept — functions can only return a single scalar value
MySQL cannot create any functions at all
MySQL functions cannot accept parameters
MySQL functions cannot be DETERMINISTIC
questions.explain: Unlike T-SQL, PL/SQL, and PostgreSQL, MySQL functions are scalar-only — there is no RETURNS TABLE or equivalent, so developers use a procedure or view instead.

questions.q: How does PL/SQL simulate a table-returning function?
options: By returning a REF CURSOR, which the caller must OPEN/FETCH from rather than query directly in a FROM clause
PL/SQL has a native RETURNS TABLE clause identical to PostgreSQL's
PL/SQL cannot return anything other than a single NUMBER
PL/SQL functions automatically convert to table-valued functions
questions.explain: A REF CURSOR is a pointer to a result set the caller fetches from explicitly — it simulates table-returning behavior but isn't directly queryable in a FROM clause like a T-SQL TVF.

questions.q: What syntax does PostgreSQL use to create a genuine table-returning function, queryable directly in a FROM clause?
options: RETURNS TABLE(...) or RETURNS SETOF sometype
RETURNS REF CURSOR
RETURNS SCALAR
PostgreSQL cannot create table-returning functions
questions.explain: PostgreSQL functions declared with RETURNS TABLE(...) or RETURNS SETOF sometype can be queried directly with SELECT * FROM FunctionName(...), much like a T-SQL table-valued function.

questions.q: Which two platforms in this lesson have functions that are directly queryable in a FROM clause, like a table?
options: T-SQL and PostgreSQL
MySQL and PL/SQL
Only MySQL
None of the four platforms support this
questions.explain: T-SQL's table-valued functions and PostgreSQL's RETURNS TABLE/SETOF functions can both be queried directly in a FROM clause; PL/SQL's REF CURSOR approach and MySQL's scalar-only functions cannot.
